channel.title: WireMinute | Breaking News & Live World Updates
channel.description: Breaking news and live world updates from WireMinute: world, politics, business, technology, sports and health, reported in our own words and updated every minute.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Shuts Key East-West Oil Pipeline After Drone Attack Launched From Iraq
item.description: Saudi Arabia has shut down its East-West oil pipeline, the kingdom's main bypass around the blocked Strait of Hormuz, after drone attacks launched from Iraq, and Baghdad has confirmed the strikes came from its territory and dismissed a military commander.

item.title: Student Deaths at India's IITs Expose Gaps in Campus Mental Health Support
item.description: A student who won a place at one of India's elite technology institutes died months later in a suspected suicide, a case that has revived hard questions about how the country's most celebrated campuses look after their brightest students.

item.title: India Says It Killed Kashmir's Last Local Militant, but Experts Say the Rebels Have Adapted
item.description: India's home minister has declared that the last local armed fighter in Indian-administered Kashmir is dead, after security forces killed a commander in a mosque siege last week, but analysts and former police officers say the armed campaign has not ended, only changed shape.

item.title: Two American Airlines Jets Clip Wings While Taxiing at Reagan National Airport
item.description: Two American Airlines passenger jets clipped wings while taxiing for departure at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport on Friday evening, shearing off a wingtip, with no injuries reported, the Federal Aviation Administration said.

item.title: Eight Killed as Peruvian Military Helicopter Crashes in Coca-Growing Valley
item.description: Eight Peruvian service members have been killed after an air force helicopter crashed in a remote coca-growing valley in the country's south-east, the defence ministry said, with the pilot the only survivor.

item.title: WWE Star Bronson Reed Dies at 38
item.description: World Wrestling Entertainment has announced the death of Jermaine Haley, the Australian wrestler known to fans as Bronson Reed, at the age of 38, saying he died on Friday due to medical complications.

item.title: US Rejects Iranian Claims of Seized Tankers, Carrier Strike and Hormuz Toll
item.description: The United States has denied claims by Iran's navy chief that American forces seized two Iranian oil tankers, that Iranian forces struck the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln, and that Washington charges ships $2.5 million to pass through the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Saudi Air Defences Intercept Houthi Cruise Missile Aimed at Riyadh
item.description: Saudi air defences have intercepted and destroyed a cruise missile launched by Yemen's Houthis towards Riyadh, the Saudi-led coalition said.

item.title: Russia Rejects Black Sea Grain-Ship Ceasefire as Ukraine Warns Food Exports Are at Risk
item.description: Russia has rejected Ukraine's proposal for a ceasefire covering grain ships in the Black Sea, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, as Moscow linked any deal to a halt in Ukrainian strikes on its oil refineries and pipelines.

item.title: Israel Says Two MSF Staff Killed in Gaza Clinic Strike Were Hamas Members
item.description: The Israeli military has said two Doctors Without Borders staff killed in a strike on the charity's Gaza City clinic were members of Hamas, as the World Health Organization condemned the attack and the charity demanded accountability.

item.title: Putin Unveils Nuclear Submarine Armed With Hypersonic Missiles
item.description: President Vladimir Putin has unveiled a new nuclear-powered submarine that Moscow says is the first equipped with Zircon hypersonic missiles, attending a flag-raising ceremony at the Sevmash shipyard in Severodvinsk on Friday as the vessel formally joined the Russian navy.

item.title: US Disables Another Ship Trying to Run Iran Blockade in Gulf of Oman
item.description: The United States said it disabled a commercial ship in the Gulf of Oman on Thursday after the vessel tried to run the naval blockade of Iranian ports, the latest ship to be stopped as Tehran vowed to break the embargo.

item.title: SAP Confirms Security Incident After Reports of Stolen GitHub Tokens and Altered Code
item.description: SAP has confirmed a security incident in its software development systems after reports that attackers stole employee access tokens and used them to copy and alter source code on GitHub, in an incident the company is tracking under the name Project Granite.

item.title: UK Benefits Staff Back Online After Cyber Incident, But Public Portals Still Down
item.description: Millions of people in Britain are still unable to reach online benefits and pension services after a serious cyber incident, though internal systems were restarted on Friday evening so staff can help callers while the public portals stay offline.

item.title: OpenAI Hits Back at Apple With Trade Secrets Countersuit in AI Device Race
item.description: OpenAI has filed a countersuit against Apple, accusing the iPhone maker of stealing its trade secrets and leaning on suppliers to slow its push into AI-powered devices, in a legal fight that pits two of the biggest names in technology against each other.

item.title: Venezuela to Repeal Law That Banned Opposition Figures From Office for Decades
item.description: Venezuela's National Assembly will move next week to repeal a 2024 law that barred opposition politicians from public office for decades if they backed foreign sanctions, the Assembly's president announced on Thursday.

item.title: Hamas Chief's Son Escapes Gaza Strike as Israel Kills Two Near Medical Clinic
item.description: Hamas leader Khalil al-Hayya's last surviving son has escaped an Israeli air strike on his family in Gaza, as Israeli attacks killed more Palestinians across the territory on Friday, including two men near a medical clinic in Gaza City.

item.title: Hackers Breach US Air Force's Main Cloud Platform, Putting Sensitive Military Data at Risk
item.description: Hackers have broken into Cloud One, the cloud system the US Air Force uses to run scores of its applications, in an intrusion found in recent weeks while the platform was being upgraded.

item.title: Kenyan Cult Leader Convicted over 123 Deaths in Shakahola Starvation Case
item.description: A court in Mombasa has convicted Kenyan preacher Paul Mackenzie of the manslaughter of 123 followers he ordered to starve themselves to death in the Shakahola forest, the final verdict in one of the deadliest cult cases of modern times.

item.title: Mexico Files Formal Complaint with US over DEA Tip Line on Alleged Drug Traffickers
item.description: Mexico has filed a formal complaint with the United States over a Drug Enforcement Administration tip line seeking information on suspected drug traffickers and allegedly corrupt Mexican officials, President Claudia Sheinbaum has said, in a fresh strain on relations between the two neighbours.

item.title: Fury Cleared to Fight Joshua on December 11 After Wife Withdraws Schizophrenia Claim
item.description: Tyson Fury has been cleared to fight Anthony Joshua in Cardiff on December 11, after his wife Paris withdrew her claim that the former world heavyweight champion had been diagnosed with schizophrenia.

item.title: Strike Kills 11 Civilians, Most of Them Children, in Yemen's Taiz
item.description: An air strike has killed 11 civilians, most of them children, in Yemen's Taiz governorate, according to media linked to the Houthi movement.

item.title: Marquez Bows Out at the Top With Shock MotoGP Retirement After Eighth Title
item.description: Eight-time MotoGP champion Marc Marquez will retire after this weekend's Valencia Grand Prix, his Ducati team announced on Friday, bringing one of motorcycle racing's greatest careers to a close at the very top.

item.title: Australia Sanctions Two Men Accused of Running Iran-Backed Arson Attacks on Synagogue and Kosher Restaurant
item.description: Australia has placed counter-terrorism financing sanctions on two men it says orchestrated antisemitic arson attacks on a Sydney kosher restaurant and a Melbourne synagogue in 2024 on behalf of Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps, naming them publicly for the first time.

item.title: News Agency AFP Takes Content Platform Offline After Cyberattack
item.description: One of the world's biggest news agencies has taken its main content platform offline after a cyberattack in the early hours of Thursday, and says it does not yet know who was behind it.

item.title: Zelenskyy Says Calling Putin a Friend Is Like Calling Hitler a Friend
item.description: Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said it is strange for Donald Trump to call Vladimir Putin his friend, likening it to calling Adolf Hitler a friend during the Second World War.

item.title: Goyal Says India-US Trade Deal Is Nearly Done as Tariff Threat Hangs Over Talks
item.description: India's commerce minister says a long-delayed trade agreement with Washington is close to being finished, days after the United States warned it would raise tariffs on Indian goods to 25 per cent if the two sides fail to agree.

item.title: UN Rapporteur Demands Costa Rica Prove Terror Claim or Apologise
item.description: Francesca Albanese, the United Nations special rapporteur for the occupied Palestinian territories, has accused Costa Rica of defamation and demanded it prove its claim that she is linked to terrorism or retract it and apologise, after the country refused her entry and held her at San Jose airport.

item.title: Ecuador Flood Toll Rises to 34 as El Niño Rains Displace About 47,000
item.description: The death toll from El Niño-linked flooding across Ecuador has risen to 34, the country's risk agency said on Friday, with about 47,000 people displaced and more than 126,000 affected in total.

item.title: Marital Rape Still Legal Across Much of South Asia, Leaving Millions of Wives Unprotected, Report Finds
item.description: Millions of married women across South Asia have no legal protection against rape by their husbands, a new regional report has found, with the law in five of the region's eight countries still treating forced sex inside marriage as no crime at all.
